findings.statement: the store is larger than the memory allowed to cache it
the default readahead does not amplify a random read
findings.detail: 10696710 device bytes per 100-byte value with the default advice against 8536 with MADV_RANDOM -- 106967.1x against 85.4x amplification. Measured from /proc/self/io with the page cache dropped first, so these are bytes the device was asked for and not bytes inferred from file size

findings.statement: telling the kernel a random read is random makes it faster
findings.detail: 8304 reads/s with MADV_RANDOM against 169 with the default (random vs default: greater 49.129x (p=0.0122, rel_iqr 28.3%/8.5%)). Major faults: 4168 against 4129 -- the proof that these passes were cold, and the count of times the engine stopped for the disk

notes: page cache dropped before every pass; read amplification measured from /proc/self/io rather than inferred. Both arms read the same file in the same process and differ only in ReadOptions::readahead
